<x_0.041><y_0.2531>_Of the_ DIFFERENT REFRANGIBILITY OF LIGHT.<x_0.7588><y_0.2719><class_Section-header>

<x_0.0068><y_0.2734>We have hitherto fuppofed that a particle of light, as it comes from the fun, is the leaft particle into which light can be separated. But we muft now correct this lup- pofition, by flewing, that a particle of light, as it comes from the fun, is, properly speaking, a bundle of rays, which may be feparated from one another. Therefore, for the future, by a ray of light we mult be underflood to mean, not that collection of particles which we have hitherto called by this name, but the lealt particles in- to which light can be feparated.<x_0.7988><y_0.4141><class_Text>

<x_0.04><y_0.418>_Rays of light are faid to, be differently refrangible, when at the fame or equal angles of incidence forms are more turned out of the way than others._<x_0.7959><y_0.4617><class_Text>

<x_0.042><y_0.4656>_Rays are faid to be differently reflexible, if fome are more easily reflected than others._<x_0.793><y_0.4961><class_Text>

<x_0.043><y_0.4992>_Light is called homogeneous, when all the rays are equally refrangible : it is called heterogeneous, when fome rays are more refrangible than others._<x_0.7939><y_0.5445><class_Text>

<x_0.0439><y_0.5469>_The colours of homogeneous light are called primary or simple colours; and thofe of heterogenous light are called secondary or mixed._<x_0.7949><y_0.5914><class_Text>

<x_0.0391><y_0.5945>_The rays of the fun are not all equally refrangible: and thofe rays, which have a different degree of refrangibility, have likewise a different colour._<x_0.791><y_0.6391><class_Text>

<x_0.0059><y_0.6422>If a beam of light SF, (No. 32.) that comes from the fun, paffes into a dark room through F a round hole in a window flutter EG ; this beam proceeding straight forwards, and falling upon a paper at Y, would there make a round picture of the fun. This picture would be a confufed one indeed, if the hole is a large one and there is no lens in the hole. However, as this round fpot of light is a picture of the fun, we shall hereafter, notwithlanding its confusion, call it by this name.
